lines.text: Fifty beats a second. Watch them.
lines.phonemes: fˈɪfti bˈiːts ɐ sˈɛkənd. wˈɑːtʃ ðˌɛm.

lines.text: No camera on Earth could film all of this. So every picture here is drawn by a computer, from the physics. Ten times slower. One second now takes ten. A small hummingbird hovers at the window. Its wings beat about fifty times a second. At ten times slower, that's five beats a second. Now you can see them. Not a blur anymore, just wings, going up and down.
lines.phonemes: nˈoʊ kˈæmɹə ˌɔn ˈɜːθ kʊd fˈɪlm ˈɔːl ʌv ðˈɪs. sˌoʊ ˈɛvɹi pˈɪktʃɚ hˈɪɹ ɪz dɹˈɔːn baɪ ɐ kəmpjˈuːɾɚ, fɹʌmðə fˈɪzɪks. tˈɛn tˈaɪmz slˈoʊɚ. wˈʌn sˈɛkənd nˈaʊ tˈeɪks tˈɛn. ɐ smˈɔːl hˈʌmɪŋbˌɜːd hˈʌvɚz æt ðə wˈɪndoʊ. ɪts wˈɪŋz bˈiːt ɐbˌaʊt fˈɪfti tˈaɪmz ɐ sˈɛkənd. æt tˈɛn tˈaɪmz slˈoʊɚ, ðæts fˈaɪv bˈiːts ɐ sˈɛkənd. nˈaʊ juː kæn sˈiː ðˌɛm. nˌɑːɾə blˈɜːɹ ˌɛnɪmˈɔːɹ, dʒˈʌst wˈɪŋz, ɡˌoʊɪŋ ˌʌp ænd dˈaʊn.

lines.text: Each wing sweeps forward, flips, and sweeps back. Watch the wing tips: they trace tiny loops in the air. Here's why they blur at full speed. Your eyes blend flashes that come faster than about sixty a second. So fifty wing beats a second just smear together. Quick pause: if that one got you, tap like and follow. Okay, back to it. But look at the fly by the cup. Even at ten times slower, its wings are still a blur.
